title: The Uniform of Vilna
premise: In 1794 Vilna, mapmaker's apprentice Mirabel Whitlock inherits her dead master's unfinished atlas — and the hidden ledger inside it, a record of names the occupying army will kill to suppress. When soldiers requisition the workshop and seize what they believe is the only copy, Mirabel must finish the atlas and smuggle the true ledger out of the city before the victors' historians rewrite the record. Betrayed by the officer she has come to love and hunted by his superior, she chooses truth over safety, completing the master's work at the cost of nearly everything. The book ends with the atlas reaching foreign presses under another's name while Mirabel, unrecognized, watches the truth finally go on the record.
about_author: Theo Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced maps and municipal records across Eastern Europe. This is their third novel of ordinary people caught in the machinery of occupation.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlives Us
chapters.summary: Mirabel Whitlock, POV. In her dead master Aldous Fenwick's workshop, Mirabel inks the final plates of his atlas of Vilna, hiding her grief in busywork. She discovers a false back panel in his drafting desk concealing a ledger of names she doesn't yet understand. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Imperial officers arrive and requisition the town — quartering, supplies, and 'all cartographic materials.' Captain Elias Voss, courteous and weary, catalogs the workshop but misses the ledger behind the panel. Mirabel lies for the first time in her life. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. By candlelight she deciphers the ledger: Fenwick recorded the executions, confiscations, and informants of the occupation, each entry keyed to atlas coordinates. She realizes the atlas itself is an index to testimony. Beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Historian's Commission
chapters.summary: Colonel Brandt, POV. The victors' official historian arrives to produce a sanctioned account of the campaign; Brandt orders all private papers seized and inconvenient witnesses 'relocated.' Voss objects quietly and is overruled. Beat: institutional evil dressed as scholarship.

chapters.title: What the Master Owed
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. She seeks out Fenwick's old friend, the printer Jozef Hala, and learns why Fenwick kept the ledger: his own brother's name is among the condemned. Hala agrees to help but warns that paper leaves trails. Beat: inheritance of a debt she never chose.

chapters.title: Quarters
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss, alternating POV. Voss is billeted near the workshop; their conversations over shared tea turn from wary to genuine. He shows her a sketch he draws of the river, confessing he once wanted to be a mapmaker too. Beat: love beginning against both their judgments.

chapters.title: The First Copyist
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. She begins copying the ledger into ciphered marginal notes on blank atlas proofs — invisible unless you know the grid. Hala's apprentice Tomas helps, ambitious and careless. Beat: craft as resistance, tension rising through small errors.

chapters.title: Relocated
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. A witness from the ledger's pages disappears overnight; Mirabel recognizes the name. She understands the clock is real: every historian's deadline costs lives. Beat: guilt and urgency entwined.

chapters.title: The River Survey
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss, POV. On a joint survey of the river fortifications, they speak plainly — she probes what he knows of the seizures; he admits doubts about the occupation but defends his oath. Each hides half a heart. Beat: intimacy built on mutual concealment.

chapters.title: Tomas Sells a Page
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Tomas trades one ciphered proof to a black-market dealer for coin; within a day, soldiers search Hala's print shop. Nothing incriminating is found — barely. Mirabel confronts Tomas; Hala forbids her from casting him out. Beat: betrayal inside the circle of trust.

chapters.title: The Sanctioned Atlas
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. The historian presents draft chapters erasing the executions entirely; Brandt demands the original survey plates be destroyed after copying so no rival version can exist. Voss volunteers to oversee it — to protect them, he tells himself. Beat: duty tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: Confession at the Drafting Table
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss, POV. Voss discovers a ciphered proof by lamplight and says nothing; instead he asks her, obliquely, whether some records deserve to survive their makers' masters. They almost tell each other everything. Beat: love and duty at open war.

chapters.title: The Burning Cart
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Soldiers burn confiscated papers in the market square; among them Mirabel spots Fenwick's early correspondence. Watching her master's life go up in smoke, she commits fully: the ledger will leave the city, whatever it costs. Beat: grief transmuted into vow.

chapters.title: Hala's Press Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Hala is arrested on suspicion of sedition; the shop is sealed with the finished ciphered plates inside. Mirabel loses her exit route, her ally, and nearly her nerve. Beat: the plan collapsing at the worst hour.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Ordered to escort Hala east and destroy the plates, Voss instead falsifies the destruction report and slips Mirabel the seal stamp needed to reopen the shop — knowing it may hang him. Beat: love choosing treason.

chapters.title: One Night in the Sealed Shop
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Using Voss's stamp, she recovers the plates and completes the atlas's final sheet — the master's last map, finished in her hand. Tomas redeems himself by holding the door against a patrol. Beat: triumph shadowed by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. Tomas's earlier sale surfaces; Brandt traces the cipher to the workshop and sets a trap for whoever comes for the rest. Voss is assigned to spring it. Beat: the net closing from every side.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dawn
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Voss, POV. Mirabel attempts to carry the atlas out with a grain convoy; Voss, ordered to stop her, lets her pass at the bridge and is seen doing it. Their farewell is three words and a lifetime. Beat: climax of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. The atlas reaches the river barge safely, but Mirabel doubles back for Hala's sake and is taken. In her cell she rehearses silence, measuring how long she can hold before the ledger's key dies with her. Beat: darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Testified
chapters.summary: Voss and Brandt, POV. Rather than let Mirabel hang alone, Voss confirms the suppressed record before the tribunal, turning his court-martial into public testimony. Brandt can bury a mapmaker, not an officer of rank. Beat: justice outside the law, spoken inside it.

chapters.title: The Record Survives Its Makers
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Months later, in a neutral port, the atlas appears from a foreign press — credited to 'the late A. Fenwick and an unnamed hand.' The executions are on the record; the historians cannot unprint it. Beat: vindication without victory.

chapters.title: The Unnamed Hand
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Released in a prisoner exchange, Mirabel returns to a ruined workshop and begins teaching apprentices — including a pardoned Tomas — to make maps that tell the truth. A letter arrives bearing Voss's familiar river sketch. Beat: quiet hope, love deferred but alive.
